newsitem.title: UK: UK's Nationwide says Sept house prices up 1.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: UK's Nationwide says Sept house prices up 1.4 pct.

text.p: The Nationwide Building Society released the following UK house price data -
HOUSE PRICES (index base Q1 1983=100) Sept Aug Sept,95

NOTE - The Nationwide said the apparent strength of the housing market continues to reflect distortions caused by shortages of quality housing in certain sectors of the market which are giving a short-term boost to prices while severely limiting sales.
But it said that property transactions have been on an upward trend so far this year and the most recent figures for August indicated levels in activity at least back to early 1995 levels.

"The strength of mortgage lending over the summer suggests this improvement will continue and should gain momentum as more existing owner-occupiers return to the market, alleviating localised supply contraints and resulting pressure on prices," said Philip Williamson, Nationwide's corporate development officer.

"The exceptional rate of growth in prices seen in recent months is, we believe, unlikely to be sustained. We need to emphasise again that the current upturn has none of the characteristics normally associated with a damaging boom," he said. -- Rosemary Bennett +44 171 542 7715
